caption: A 3x2 loop: observer O1 (1,0) watches O5 (2,0) and powers lamp L (0,0) behind it; O2 (0,1) watches L, O3 (1,1) watches O2, O4 (2,1) watches O3, O5 (2,0) watches O4. The lamp goes dark 4 gt after its power ends, so O2 sees two edges per pass.
Two observers face to face: each watches the other, so every output change of one is a shape update in front of the other. Kicked by placing the second observer (B) last.
Four observers in a horizontal square, each watching the previous one (A <- D <- C <- B <- A): one 2 gt pulse travels around, 2 gt per observer. Kicked by placing B last.
Six observers around a 3x2 rectangle, each watching the previous one. Kicked by placing B last.

Torch + delay-1 repeater loop (draft, clk-rt): T (wall torch on A) -> 3 dust -> repeater R -> A. Inner loop period 4 * (1 + 1) = 8 gt: 7 x 8 = 56 <= 60, so the torch burns out at its 8th turn-off; R keeps T's input powered past that turn-off, so the 160 gt burnout re-check is not replaced by a relight tick, and T relights 160 gt after its 8th turn-off. Predicted period 220.

BURNOUT clock, 9 blocks (clk-rt): the 9-block torch + repeater loop with a delay-1 repeater. Inner loop period 8 (7 x 8 = 56 <= 60): the torch burns out at its 8th turn-off and relights 160 gt later (the repeater still powers it at that turn-off): period 4 + 56 + 160 = 220.

Comparator subtract clock, 8 blocks (draft, clk-rt): rear = redstone block (15); the output strongly powers block A; dust beside A carries A's strength to the comparator's side. Expected: output 15 / 1 alternating every 2 gt (period 4); the side dust 14 / 0.
Comparator subtract clock (draft, clk-rt): rear = redstone block (15), output -> 3 dust -> side. Expected: output alternates 15 / 2 every 2 gt (period 4), the last dust 13 / 0.

Torch + repeater loop, 9 blocks (draft, clk-rt): wall torch T on A -> repeater R reads T directly -> R strongly powers F -> dust beside F -> dust pointing into A. One inversion, loop delay 2 + 2d: period 4 (1 + d) = 12 with the delay-2 repeater (16 / 20 with delay 3 / 4).
C -> repeater(4) -> dust -> dust -> repeater(1) -> piston behind C: retraction at A+20, dist 1.

Self-starting: R is placed powered with no input; its turn-off is the first observer pulse. Calibrated sensor C strongly powers the stone below it; repeater R (delay 4) reads that stone; observer O (above R) watches R and plays note block N (diagonal to C: dist sqrt2, travel 1).
C -> repeater (4) -> stone X -> wall torch T on X's north face -> note block N diagonal to C.
Self-starting: R is placed powered with no input; its turn-off is the first observer pulse. Calibrated sensor C -> repeater R (delay 4) -> observer O watching R -> note block N (dist sqrt5).
Self-starting: calibrated C -> repeater R (delay 4, placed powered) -> observer O watching R -> note block N in line (dist 3 from C): event at A+20, travel 3.
Self-starting: fence gate E placed open+powered with no power closes on its placement update (BLOCK_CLOSE); then observer O's 3rd pulse on C opens it each period.
Self-starting: iron trapdoor placed open+powered with no power closes on its placement update.
Self-starting: piston placed extended (with its head) and unpowered retracts on its placement update (BLOCK_DEACTIVATE); then O's 3rd pulse on C moves it each period.

Self-starting 3-block clock: calibrated C, observer O watching C, oak trapdoor E behind O placed open+powered with no power: it closes on its placement update (BLOCK_CLOSE wakes C); then O's pulses at A+2, A+12, A+22 open/close E and only the A+22 one is heard (C re-arms at A+20).
Calibrated sensor C watched by observer O, note block N behind O (dist 2 from C).
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, piston E behind O (dist 2): O's 3rd pulse (A+22) extends E.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, sticky piston E behind O (dist 2), facing away.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, stone strongly powered by O, note block beyond it (dist 3).
C, observer O watching C, observer Q watching O (sideways), note block N behind Q (dist sqrt5): Q's 3rd pulse at A+24.
C, two observers in line, note block N (dist 3): 3rd pulse at A+24, travel 3.
C, three observers curling back (O watches C, Q watches O, R watches Q), note block N diagonal to C: A+26, travel 1.
Calibrated C, observer O watching C, EMPTY dispenser behind O: it fires 4 gt after each rising edge (empty dispense = BLOCK_ACTIVATE); the A+22 pulse fires it at A+26, heard at dist 2.
Plain sensor C (30 active + 10 cooldown), observer O watching C, note block behind O (dist 2): O's pulse after C's COOLDOWN->INACTIVE (A+42) plays the note.
Plain sensor C, observer O watching C, empty dispenser behind O (fires 4 gt after O's A+42 pulse).

Pure vibration ring (nothing but sensors changes state): calibrated sensors S1 (1,0,0), S2 (15,0,8), S3 (1,0,16), each with an amethyst block beside it; when S_i activates its amethyst resonates and S_(i+1) hears it floor(dist) = 15 gt later. P = 3 x 15. A1 is out of S3's range (dist^2 257), so after the kick only S2 wakes; afterwards the sensor two hops ahead is always still in its 20 gt dead time. Kick: right-click the note block K (only S1 is within 16 of it; S1 faces east so its back, K, gets no power from it).

Hopper slosh, 4 blocks (clk-item): two hoppers facing each other hold one item; it hops back and forth, 7 gt per hop (the receiving hopper was empty: TransferCooldown 8 - 1). A comparator reading the west hopper is on 7 gt, off 7 gt. redsim: P=14 gt, warmup 3, family comparator+hopper, 4 blocks, output on 7/14 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Ring lock, 10 blocks (clk-item): 8 hoppers around a 3x3 square with a comparator in the middle that reads the west hopper and points into the east one, locking it whenever the west one holds an item; 4 swords. The lock makes the items queue and overtake: period 15 gt. redsim: P=15 gt, warmup 122, family comparator+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 7/15 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Ring lock, 10 blocks (clk-item): 8 hoppers around a 3x3 square, a comparator in the middle reads the west hopper and locks the east one (it points into it); 3 items (2 stone + 1 sword). Items queue at the locked hopper and are released in an irregular order: the whole pattern repeats only every 654 gt. redsim: P=654 gt, warmup 22, family comparator+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 234/654 gt, 30 rising edge(s)

Dropper ring, 10 blocks (clk-item): hoppers and droppers around a 3x3 square, each passing items to the next; a comparator in the middle reads one ring container and points into the opposite one, a dropper: each time an item arrives under the comparator, the dropper fires 4 gt later (rising edge) and pushes one item on. Items wait in the droppers for a trigger, so the cycle is not a multiple of 7: 20 gt. redsim: P=20 gt, warmup 34, family comparator+dropper+hopper, 10 blocks, output on 7/20 gt, 1 rising edge(s)

Jukebox carousel, 9 blocks (clk-item): 3 copies of disc 11 go around a jukebox J. A playing jukebox emits 15: it locks the extractor hopper below it, powers the inserter dropper beside it, keeps the torch standing on it off, and lights a 2-dust line whose second dust sits on a note block next to the lift dropper. When the song ends (lengthInTicks + 20 gt) the extractor pushes its waiting disc into the lift and pulls the played one; the torch relights 2 gt later and fires the inserter through the cell above it (4 gt): the next disc goes in. The new song lights the dust, the note block flips and fires the lift 4 gt later: the waiting disc rises into the inserter. Period = song + 6 gt, whatever the hopper tick order.
